heading: Mapping: Yon
summary: Converter signatures generate mappings from a literal JSON field plan or from declared source and target model types. Explicit fields override inferred same-named model fields.
body:
GET /catalog returns {"summary":{"productId":7,"title":"Anvil","absent":null,"kind":"product"}}. Converter is the role. A converter copies values from its input into a new output shape. It is a <Name>Converter type in server/converters. A controller or service asks for it with Needs, like a MapStruct mapper that Spring injects: a Needs field, a constructor parameter in F#, or Needs above an attr_reader in Ruby. In JavaScript and Ruby the field name names the provider (productConverter, product_converter). Lua names it in the type comment above the field, `---@type ProductConverter`. A converter needs no behavior context and no Setup, because a mapping reads only its argument, so Tachyon builds it with no constructor argument. Convert describes the whole method. Each entry names its target (the output field). Each entry takes either a source path of at most eight names joined by dots, or a literal constant. The method takes exactly one parameter, the value it converts, and the plan reads it. The parameter and the result keep the language's JSON value type. A source that is missing maps to null, exactly as in MapStruct. An input field that no entry names is dropped, so extra never reaches the output. A Convert has at most 32 entries. Options that are not one strict JSON object fail the build, and a note after the closing bracket is not part of the options. Writing the same target twice fails the build.

A Converter is a contract, like a MapStruct @Mapper interface: it has no implementation, and Tachyon generates each mapping. It is an interface in Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, PHP and Go, and an interface of `abstract` members in F#. It is a trait in Rust, an abstract interface class in Dart and a Protocol class in Python. Python writes the stub (the empty body) as an Ellipsis. JavaScript, Ruby and Lua have no method without a body. TypeScript cannot put a decorator on an abstract member. So these four keep an empty body. JavaScript and TypeScript declare the answer as Promise<BehaviorJsonObject | void> for the same reason. In every case, the compiler writes the class and each method, and the class has no constructor argument. So the source declares nothing else. A method body, a field, a constructor, or a class where the language has a contract form fails the build with TY1308 ("A Converter has no implementation: Tachyon generates each mapping."). `ty migrate fix --write` rewrites a class converter as a contract. `ty migrate` reports code that still builds a converter with a context, such as `new ProductConverter(context)` or `Behaviors.construct(ProductConverter, ...)`: remove it and ask for the converter with Needs.

Typed model signatures may omit Convert: Tachyon infers exact same-named target fields from models in the realm models folder and projects nested models and lists. Explicit Convert fields override their named targets; missing or incompatible target fields fail the build. JavaScript uses JSDoc parameter, return and typedef model types. JSON-value signatures keep the complete literal field plan shown here. The next sections show converters with typed models in every language, Lua included.

C++ has no tab here, because C++ Yon code has only route controllers so far: the build refuses `Converter` in C++ with `TY1308` (ADR 0099).
